docs.title: strawberry-alchemy
docs.text: Batteries-included toolkit for building Strawberry GraphQL APIs backed by SQLAlchemy. It turns the incoming selection set into one optimized query (defer unrequested columns, selectinload nested relations, SQL annotations) and ships the surrounding cast: filters, Relay pagination, repositories, row-level ACL, permissions helpers, and input/output mapping.

docs.title: What it gives you
docs.text: Area What it does QueryOptimizer Selection set → one SQLAlchemy query: selectinload, defer(), EXISTS / COUNT / ancestry CTE annotations @optimize_field hints PrefetchRelated, SelectColumns, AnnotateExists, AnnotateAnyExists, AnnotateCount, AnnotateCustom, AnnotateAncestry FilterBuilder Strawberry filter inputs → WHERE, with AND / OR, relation joins, CUSTOM_FILTERS, JSONB key filters Types BaseNodeType (Relay Node), ListResult, OptimizedListConnection / Edge / PageInfo Repository Async CRUD, soft-delete, relation add/remove, DeletionReport / cascade handlers Mapping & schema BaseSchema, schema_from_input / from_input, SQLAlchemy → Strawberry mapping Access control AccessControlFilter (row ACL), RelationAccessFilter (per-edge ACL override) Permissions Auth helpers + prepare_mutation_resources for mutation loaders Postgres RLS Session GUC helpers for app-owned CREATE POLICY DDL Models Base (+ optional SoftDeleteMixin)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python >= 3.13
  • strawberry-graphql >= 0.339.1
  • sqlalchemy[asyncio] >= 2.1.6
  • pydantic >= 2.14

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install strawberry-alchemy
# or
uv add strawberry-alchemy

docs.title: How the pieces fit together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Client[GraphQL client] --> Resolver[resolve_list / resolve_connection]
  Resolver --> Opt[QueryOptimizer]
  Opt --> ACL[AccessControlFilter]
  Opt --> Filters[FilterBuilder]
  Opt --> Hints["@optimize_field hints"]
  Opt --> SQL[SQLAlchemy query]
  SQL --> Map[map_sqlalchemy_to_type]
  Map --> Type[BaseNodeType]
  1. Subclass BaseNodeType, declare an access_filter, and field the columns / relationships the client may select.
  2. Query resolvers call resolve_node / resolve_list / resolve_connection. Those methods read info, build one optimized query, apply ACL + filters, and map rows back to Strawberry types.
  3. Computed fields use @optimize_field(...) so the optimizer knows what SQL to emit (EXISTS, counts, prefetches, …).
  4. Mutations use BaseRepository + BaseSchema / schema_from_input, optionally with prepare_mutation_resources and a BaseDeletionHandler.

Walk through a full blog API in Getting started. Production wrapping patterns (project repositories, tenancy, custom order) live in Recipes.

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text: FilterBuilder turns Strawberry filter inputs (and plain dicts) into SQLAlchemy WHERE clauses. Filters support nested AND / OR, relationship traversal, custom callables, and Postgres JSONB operators.

docs.title: Operator inputs
docs.text:
Import from strawberry_alchemy (or strawberry_alchemy.filtering):

Input Typical operators IDFilter exact, in_, not_in_, isnull StringFilter exact, iexact, contains, icontains, startswith, istartswith, endswith, iendswith, in_, not_in_, isnull IntFilter exact, gt, ge, lt, le, in_, not_in_, isnull, range BooleanFilter exact, isnull DateFilter exact, ge, gt, lt, le, in_, not_in_, isnull, range (ISO date strings; for SQL Date columns) DateTimeFilter same comparison set as DateFilter (ISO datetimes; for DateTime columns) EnumFilter[T] exact, in_, not_in_, isnull JSONFilter jsonb_contains, jsonb_contained_by, jsonb_has_key, jsonb_has_any, jsonb_has_all, jsonb_path, isnull

GraphQL field names use trailing underscores where needed (in_, not_in_); FilterBuilder maps them to lookups in / not_in.

Boolean operator values such as isnull: true are not coerced to the column type (fixed in 0.7.2), so DateTimeFilter(isnull=True) works.

docs.title: Composing a filter input
docs.text:
import strawberry
from strawberry_alchemy import DateFilter, IDFilter, StringFilter


@strawberry.input
class PostFilter:
    title: StringFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET
    user_id: IDFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET
    published_on: DateFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET
    AND: list[PostFilter] | None = strawberry.UNSET
    OR: list[PostFilter] | None = strawberry.UNSET

Example GraphQL:

query {
  posts {
    list(filters: {
      OR: [
        { title: { icontains: "alchemy" } }
        { userId: { exact: "…" } }
      ]
    }) {
      items { id title }
      totalCount
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Relationship filters
docs.text: Nested filter objects on relationship field names become joins. The related model's columns use the same operator inputs.

docs.title: Custom filters (CUSTOM_FILTERS)
docs.text:
For non-column keys (full-text shortcuts, office “tabs”, etc.), register callables on the GraphQL type:

from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any, ClassVar

def _title_search_filter(model: type[Any], value: Any) -> Any:
    term = f"%{value}%"
    return or_(model.title.ilike(term), model.body.ilike(term))


@strawberry.type
class PostType(BaseNodeType):
    access_filter: ClassVar[...] = PostAccessFilter
    CUSTOM_FILTERS: ClassVar[dict[str, Callable[..., Any]]] = {
        "title_search": _title_search_filter,
    }

The filter input exposes title_search: str | None; FilterBuilder invokes the callable instead of treating it as a column.

Older apps

Pre-0.2 code sometimes used _custom_filters_registry directly. Prefer CUSTOM_FILTERS on the type; the registry is wired automatically.

docs.title: JSONB key filters (Postgres)
docs.text:
Nested keys under a JSON/JSONB column compile to column['key'].astext lookups. Partial JSONB selections stay undeferred and trim output keys to the selection tree.

@strawberry.input
class LocalizedStringFilter:
    cs: StringFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET
    en: StringFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET


@strawberry.input
class ListingFilter:
    title: LocalizedStringFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET  # JSONB column

JSONFilter covers containment / key existence operators on the whole document.

docs.title: AccessControlFilter
docs.text:
Row-level ACL applied to root queries, totalCount, and nested selectinloads for that model. Subclass names must end with AccessFilter.

class PostAccessFilter(AccessControlFilter):
    model_class = Post

    @staticmethod
    async def apply_filter(query: Any, model: type[Any], context_user: Any) -> Any:
        if context_user is None:
            return query.where(False)
        return query.where(model.user_id == context_user.id)

Attach via BaseNodeType.access_filter ClassVar, or pass access_filter= into resolve_* / PrefetchRelated.

This is application SQL ACL, orthogonal to Postgres RLS policies — see Postgres RLS and Recipes.

docs.title: RelationAccessFilter
docs.text:
FieldExtension for when a nested edge needs a different ACL than the model's default registry entry (e.g. reporting-line manager still readable when people-scope employment ACL would hide them).

from strawberry_alchemy import RelationAccessFilter


@strawberry.type
class EmploymentType(BaseNodeType):
    ...
    manager: PersonType | None = strawberry.field(
        default=strawberry.UNSET,
        extensions=[RelationAccessFilter(ManagerPersonAccessFilter)],
    )

Optional foreign_key= enables a mutation to_type() fallback: if the relationship attribute is missing but the FK is set, load via resolve_nodes with the edge ACL.

extensions=[RelationAccessFilter(ManagerPersonAccessFilter, foreign_key="manager_id")]

The override is edge-local — it does not overwrite the model-keyed ACL registry used by other edges or root queries.

PrefetchRelated(..., access_filter=...) provides the same edge-local ACL for @optimize_field prefetches (AND-ed with any filter / filter_current_user conditions).

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
This walkthrough builds a minimal blog API (Post / Comment) with strawberry-alchemy.

A complete, importable version lives in examples/blog and is covered by make test ARGS="tests/examples". Prefer that tree when you want copy-pasteable modules that stay in sync with the library.

The app exposes: a Relay node query, a filtered list query, a Relay connection query, and create / update / delete mutations.

docs.title: Context contract
docs.text:
Every resolver that uses BaseNodeType.resolve_* expects info.context to provide:

Attribute Role async get_session() -> AsyncSession DB session for the request identity (awaitable) or user Current user for ACL / permissions db_execution_lock asyncio.Lock serializing optimizer DB work on the shared session 
# context.py
import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession


@dataclass
class ExampleUser:
    id: UUID
    role: str = "user"


@dataclass
class ExampleContext:
    session: AsyncSession
    user: ExampleUser | None
    db_execution_lock: asyncio.Lock = field(default_factory=asyncio.Lock)

    async def get_session(self) -> AsyncSession:
        return self.session

    @property
    def identity(self) -> Any:
        async def _identity() -> ExampleUser | None:
            return self.user

        return _identity()

Wire this into your ASGI / FastAPI context getter the same way you would any Strawberry context.

docs.title: 1. Models
docs.text:
The library Base uses Postgres UUID dialect types. For SQLite tests (as in the blog example), define your own declarative base with sqlalchemy.Uuid and the same id / created_at / updated_at columns. Soft-delete is optional via SoftDeleteMixin.

# models.py
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

from sqlalchemy import DateTime, ForeignKey, String, Uuid, func
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship

from strawberry_alchemy import SoftDeleteMixin


class ExampleBase(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class Post(SoftDeleteMixin, ExampleBase):
    __tablename__ = "post"

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(Uuid, primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
    user_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(Uuid, index=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255))
    body: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=func.now())
    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=func.now(), onupdate=func.now()
    )
    comments: Mapped[list["Comment"]] = relationship(back_populates="post")


class Comment(ExampleBase):
    __tablename__ = "comment"

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(Uuid, primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
    post_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(Uuid, ForeignKey("post.id"), index=True)
    body: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=func.now())
    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=func.now(), onupdate=func.now()
    )
    post: Mapped[Post] = relationship(back_populates="comments")

docs.title: 2. Access filters
docs.text:
Every BaseNodeType needs an AccessControlFilter subclass (name must end with AccessFilter). It is applied to root queries and nested selectinloads for that model.

# access_filters.py
from typing import Any

from strawberry_alchemy import AccessControlFilter

from .models import Comment, Post


class PostAccessFilter(AccessControlFilter):
    model_class = Post

    @staticmethod
    async def apply_filter(query: Any, model: type[Any], context_user: Any) -> Any:
        if context_user is None:
            return query.where(False)
        return query.where(model.user_id == context_user.id)


class CommentAccessFilter(AccessControlFilter):
    model_class = Comment

    @staticmethod
    async def apply_filter(query: Any, model: type[Any], context_user: Any) -> Any:
        if context_user is None:
            return query.where(False)
        return query.join(Post, model.post_id == Post.id).where(Post.user_id == context_user.id)

docs.title: 3. Filter inputs
docs.text:
Compose operator inputs (StringFilter, IDFilter, …) into a @strawberry.input. AND / OR lists nest; non-column fields can be handled via CUSTOM_FILTERS on the type (see next section).

# filters.py
import strawberry

from strawberry_alchemy import IDFilter, StringFilter


@strawberry.input
class PostFilter:
    title: StringFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET
    body: StringFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET
    user_id: IDFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET
    title_search: str | None = strawberry.UNSET
    AND: list["PostFilter"] | None = strawberry.UNSET
    OR: list["PostFilter"] | None = strawberry.UNSET

docs.title: 4. GraphQL types
docs.text:
# types.py
from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Annotated, Any, ClassVar

import strawberry
from sqlalchemy import or_
from strawberry.types import Info

from strawberry_alchemy import AnnotateExists, BaseNodeType, optimize_field

from .access_filters import CommentAccessFilter, PostAccessFilter


def _title_search_filter(model: type[Any], value: Any) -> Any:
    term = f"%{value}%"
    return or_(model.title.ilike(term), model.body.ilike(term))


@strawberry.type
class CommentType(BaseNodeType):
    access_filter: ClassVar[type[CommentAccessFilter]] = CommentAccessFilter

    post_id: uuid.UUID | None = strawberry.UNSET
    body: str | None = strawberry.UNSET
    post: Annotated[PostType | None, strawberry.lazy(".types")] = strawberry.UNSET


@strawberry.type
class PostType(BaseNodeType):
    access_filter: ClassVar[type[PostAccessFilter]] = PostAccessFilter
    CUSTOM_FILTERS: ClassVar[dict[str, Callable[..., Any]]] = {
        "title_search": _title_search_filter,
    }

    user_id: uuid.UUID | None = strawberry.UNSET
    title: str | None = strawberry.UNSET
    body: str | None = strawberry.UNSET
    comments: list[Annotated[CommentType, strawberry.lazy(".types")]] | None = strawberry.UNSET

    @strawberry.field
    @optimize_field(AnnotateExists("comments"))
    async def has_comments(self, info: Info) -> bool:
        return bool(getattr(self, "_comments_exists", False))

Scalar / relationship fields default to strawberry.UNSET so unrequested values are not required on construction. BaseNodeType already provides Relay id, created_at, and updated_at.

docs.title: 5. Queries
docs.text:
# queries.py
import strawberry
from strawberry.relay import GlobalID
from strawberry.types import Info

from strawberry_alchemy import ListResult, OptimizedListConnection

from .filters import PostFilter
from .types import PostType


@strawberry.type
class PostQueries:
    @strawberry.field
    async def node(self, info: Info, id: GlobalID) -> PostType | None:
        return await PostType.resolve_node(node_id=id.node_id, info=info)

    @strawberry.field
    async def list(
        self,
        info: Info,
        limit: int | None = None,
        offset: int | None = None,
        filters: PostFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET,
    ) -> ListResult[PostType]:
        return await PostType.resolve_list(
            info=info, limit=limit, offset=offset, filters=filters
        )

    @strawberry.field
    async def connection(
        self,
        info: Info,
        after: str | None = None,
        before: str | None = None,
        first: int | None = None,
        last: int | None = None,
        filters: PostFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET,
    ) -> OptimizedListConnection[PostType]:
        return await PostType.resolve_connection(
            info=info,
            after=after,
            before=before,
            first=first,
            last=last,
            filters=filters,
        )


@strawberry.type
class Query:
    @strawberry.field
    def posts(self) -> PostQueries:
        return PostQueries()

docs.title: 6. Schemas and repositories
docs.text:
# schemas.py
import uuid
from datetime import datetime

from strawberry_alchemy import BaseSchema


class CommentSchema(BaseSchema):
    id: uuid.UUID | None = None
    post_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
    body: str


class PostSchema(BaseSchema):
    id: uuid.UUID | None = None
    user_id: uuid.UUID
    title: str
    body: str
    deleted_at: datetime | None = None
    comments: list[CommentSchema] | None = None

# repositories.py
from typing import ClassVar

from strawberry_alchemy import BaseRepository

from .models import Comment, Post
from .schemas import CommentSchema, PostSchema


class PostRepository(BaseRepository[Post, PostSchema]):
    model_cls: ClassVar[type[Post]] = Post
    schema_cls: ClassVar[type[PostSchema]] = PostSchema
    relation_models: ClassVar[dict[str, type]] = {"comments": Comment}
    soft_delete_field: ClassVar[str | None] = "deleted_at"


class CommentRepository(BaseRepository[Comment, CommentSchema]):
    model_cls: ClassVar[type[Comment]] = Comment
    schema_cls: ClassVar[type[CommentSchema]] = CommentSchema

With ClassVars set, callers use PostRepository(session) without repeating model / schema types.

docs.title: 7. Deletion handler
docs.text:
# deletion.py
import uuid

from sqlalchemy import delete, select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from strawberry_alchemy import BaseDeletionHandler, DependentMap

from .models import Comment, Post


class PostDeletionHandler(BaseDeletionHandler[Post]):
    async def collect_dependents(
        self, session: AsyncSession, entity_id: uuid.UUID, instance: Post
    ) -> DependentMap:
        rows = (
            await session.execute(select(Comment.id).where(Comment.post_id == entity_id))
        ).scalars().all()
        return {"comments": list(rows)}

    async def handle_cascade(
        self, session: AsyncSession, entity_id: uuid.UUID, dependents: DependentMap
    ) -> None:
        comment_ids = dependents.get("comments") or []
        if comment_ids:
            await session.execute(delete(Comment).where(Comment.id.in_(comment_ids)))

docs.title: 8. Mutations
docs.text:
# mutations.py
import strawberry
from strawberry.relay import GlobalID
from strawberry.types import Info

from strawberry_alchemy import IsAuthenticated, OwnerPermission, prepare_mutation_resources

from .deletion import PostDeletionHandler
from .repositories import PostRepository
from .schemas import PostSchema
from .types import PostType


@strawberry.input
class CreatePostInput:
    title: str
    body: str


@strawberry.input
class UpdatePostInput:
    id: GlobalID
    title: str
    body: str


@strawberry.input
class DeletePostInput:
    id: GlobalID


@strawberry.type
class PostMutations:
    @strawberry.mutation
    async def create_post(self, info: Info, input: CreatePostInput) -> PostType:
        session = await info.context.get_session()
        user = await info.context.identity
        schema = PostSchema.from_input(input, user_id=user.id)
        created = await PostRepository(session).create(schema=schema)
        return created.to_type(PostType)

    @strawberry.mutation
    async def update_post(self, info: Info, input: UpdatePostInput) -> PostType:
        session = await info.context.get_session()
        schema = PostSchema.from_input(
            input, user_id=(await info.context.identity).id
        )
        result = await PostRepository(session).update(schema=schema)
        return result.to_type(PostType)

    @strawberry.mutation
    async def delete_post(self, info: Info, input: DeletePostInput) -> bool:
        session = await info.context.get_session()
        repo = PostRepository(session, deletion_handler=PostDeletionHandler())
        schema = PostSchema.from_input(input)
        await prepare_mutation_resources(
            info,
            {"post_id": input.id},
            loaders={"post_id": lambda value: repo.get_by_id(value)},
            permissions=[
                IsAuthenticated(),
                OwnerPermission(owner_field="user_id", resource_key="post_id"),
            ],
        )
        report = await repo.delete(id=schema.id, strict=False)
        return not report.has_failures

from_input / schema_from_input copy same-named fields, decode GlobalID → UUID, skip UNSET, and let kwargs (like user_id) win.

docs.title: 9. Schema
docs.text:
# schema.py
import strawberry

from .mutations import Mutation
from .queries import Query

schema = strawberry.Schema(query=Query, mutation=Mutation)

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Types and models — Base, connections, ordering
  • Filtering — operators, JSONB, RelationAccessFilter
  • Query optimizer — all @optimize_field hints
  • Recipes — production wrapping patterns

docs.title: Mapping and schema
docs.text: This page covers the Pydantic DTO layer (BaseSchema) and the helpers that map SQLAlchemy instances into Strawberry types while respecting the selection tree.

docs.title: BaseSchema
docs.text:
Pydantic model configured with from_attributes=True, safe to validate from ORM instances and from GraphQL inputs.

from strawberry_alchemy import BaseSchema
import uuid


class PostSchema(BaseSchema):
    id: uuid.UUID | None = None
    user_id: uuid.UUID
    title: str
    body: str

docs.title: dump_for_db
docs.text:
data = schema.dump_for_db(exclude={"comments"})

model_dump(exclude_unset=True) plus dropping any remaining strawberry.UNSET values — suitable for session.merge / column assignment.

docs.title: to_type
docs.text:
post_type = schema.to_type(PostType)
# or with overrides:
post_type = schema.to_type(PostType, title="Override")

Prefers PostType.from_schema(schema, **kwargs) when available; otherwise constructs from dumped fields. Nested BaseSchema values (and lists of them) become related Strawberry types, including Annotated / strawberry.lazy fields. Cyclic back-references resolve to None.

docs.title: from_input / schema_from_input
docs.text:
Build a schema (or any Pydantic BaseModel) from a Strawberry input object:

from strawberry_alchemy import schema_from_input

schema = PostSchema.from_input(input, user_id=actor.id)
# equivalent:
schema = schema_from_input(PostSchema, input, user_id=actor.id)

Rules:

  • Same-named fields are copied
  • relay.GlobalID → uuid.UUID (lists decoded item-wise)
  • Omitted / UNSET fields keep model defaults
  • Explicit None is preserved
  • Keyword arguments always win (inject actor_user_id, company_id, …)

Use plain BaseModel command objects via schema_from_input in application adapters when you do not want BaseSchema.

docs.title: SQLAlchemy → Strawberry mapping
docs.text:
Used by resolve_* after the optimizer runs:

from strawberry_alchemy import map_sqlalchemy_to_type, map_sqlalchemy_list_to_types

item = await map_sqlalchemy_to_type(instance, info, PostType, selected_fields)
items = await map_sqlalchemy_list_to_types(instances, info, PostType, selected_fields)

Only requested fields are populated; nested selections drive nested mapping.

docs.title: Submodule helpers (strawberry_alchemy.mapping)
docs.text:
Helper Role map_sqlalchemy_to_type_with_path Mapping at a nested field path extract_fields_at_path / extract_nested_fields Selection-tree slicing get_graphql_type_from_sqlalchemy Resolve GraphQL type for an instance register_global_id_type / clear_global_id_type_registry Encode-side registry for non-*_id FK fields create_global_id_from_field Build a GlobalID from a registered field 
from strawberry_alchemy.mapping import register_global_id_type

register_global_id_type("author", "User")

Register once at startup when foreign keys do not follow the *_id naming convention the default encoder expects.

docs.title: Mutation flow (typical)
docs.text:
session = await info.context.get_session()
schema = PostSchema.from_input(input, user_id=(await info.context.identity).id)
created = await PostRepository(session).create(schema=schema)
return created.to_type(PostType)

For deletes / updates that need permission checks first, see Permissions (prepare_mutation_resources).

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The strawberry_alchemy.permissions module provides Strawberry-compatible permission check classes (plain objects with has_permission) and helpers for loading mutation targets into a resource bag before checking them.

What production apps typically do

Many codebases keep field-level GraphQL auth on Strawberry's own BasePermission (or an app equivalent) and still use prepare_mutation_resources / the resource bag for mutation-time ownership checks. Using the library permission classes is optional.

docs.title: Permission classes
docs.text: All expose has_permission(self, info, **kwargs) -> bool and a message on deny. Helpers raise PermissionError when a check fails.

docs.title: IsAuthenticated
docs.text: Requires a non-null current user on the context (identity / current_user / user, depending on what your context provides).

docs.title: RolePermission(role=...)
docs.text: Requires user.role == role (see UserLike protocol: id, role).

docs.title: OwnerPermission(owner_field="user_id", resource_key=...)
docs.text: Compares the current user's id to getattr(resource, owner_field). Pass resource_key when using a ResourceInstances bag.

docs.title: ObjectAccessPermission(access_field="allowed_user_ids", resource_key=...)
docs.text: Allows access when the current user id is in a collection field on the resource.

docs.title: Resource bag and mutation helpers
docs.text:
from strawberry_alchemy import (
    IsAuthenticated,
    OwnerPermission,
    ResourceInstances,
    extract_global_ids_from_info,
    fetch_and_check_permissions,
    map_ids_to_models,
    prepare_mutation_resources,
)

docs.title: prepare_mutation_resources
docs.text:
One-shot helper for mutation resolvers:

  1. Decode GlobalIDs from input_data
  2. Load models via loaders
  3. Run permissions against the bag
  4. Return ResourceInstances
await prepare_mutation_resources(
    info,
    {"post_id": input.id},
    loaders={"post_id": lambda value: repo.get_by_id(value)},
    permissions=[
        IsAuthenticated(),
        OwnerPermission(owner_field="user_id", resource_key="post_id"),
    ],
)

Optional id_fields= overrides which keys are treated as IDs (default: keys ending with _id).

docs.title: Lower-level pieces
docs.text: Helper Role extract_global_ids_from_info(data, id_fields=None) GlobalID / strings → UUIDs map_ids_to_models(ids, loaders, bag=None) Fill a ResourceInstances bag fetch_and_check_permissions(info, permissions, resource_instances=None) Run checks; raise on deny ResourceInstances add / add_list / get / get_id / all

docs.title: BasePermissionResolver
docs.text:
ABC for apps that map an operation name (+ data) to a list of permission objects:

class PostPermissionResolver(BasePermissionResolver):
    def resolve(self, operation: str, *, data=None, **kwargs):
        if operation == "delete":
            return [IsAuthenticated(), OwnerPermission(resource_key="post_id")]
        return [IsAuthenticated()]

docs.title: Protocols
docs.text:
Protocol Shape HasId .id IdentityLike .id UserLike .id, .role PermissionContextLike .current_user, .identity ModelRegistryLike .get_model(label)

These exist so permission helpers stay typed without depending on your User model class.

docs.title: Postgres RLS session context
docs.text:
strawberry-alchemy does not invent CREATE POLICY DDL. Policies stay app-owned. This package only sets transaction-local GUCs that policies can read via current_setting(...).

Row SQL ACL via AccessControlFilter is a separate layer — many apps use both (Alchemy filters for GraphQL-shaped rules, Postgres RLS as a hard tenancy boundary). See Recipes.

docs.title: Helpers
docs.text:
from strawberry_alchemy import apply_rls_context, clear_rls_context, set_rls_guc

# Single setting (becomes app.company_id unless name already contains a dot)
await set_rls_guc(session, "company_id", str(company_id))

# Batch
await apply_rls_context(session, {"company_id": company_id, "user_id": user_id})

# Clear (sets NULL locally)
await clear_rls_context(session, ["company_id", "user_id"])

All use set_config(..., is_local=true) so values do not leak past the transaction. Target may be an AsyncSession or AsyncConnection.

Default prefix is app (DEFAULT_GUC_PREFIX). Pass prefix= to override. Bare names become app.<name>; dotted names are used as-is.

docs.title: Sample policy
docs.text:
ALTER TABLE employment ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY employment_tenant ON employment
  USING (company_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.company_id', true), '')::uuid);

Application code at the start of a request / unit of work:

async with session.begin():
    await apply_rls_context(session, {"company_id": ctx.company_id})
    ...

docs.title: CI
docs.text: Postgres-backed tests live under tests/postgres/ and run with make test-postgres (GitHub Actions Postgres 16 service in CI).

docs.title: Queries
docs.text: BaseNodeType ships four classmethods that turn the GraphQL selection set into one optimized SQLAlchemy query and map rows back to Strawberry types. Each registers the type's access_filter with the optimizer automatically.

docs.title: Context prerequisites
docs.text: Resolvers need the context contract: get_session(), identity / user, and db_execution_lock.

docs.title: resolve_node
docs.text:
Fetch a single row by UUID string (usually GlobalID.node_id).

@strawberry.field
async def node(self, info: Info, id: GlobalID) -> PostType | None:
    return await PostType.resolve_node(node_id=id.node_id, info=info)

Optional per-call override:

await PostType.resolve_node(
    node_id=id.node_id,
    info=info,
    access_filter=AdminPostAccessFilter,
)

Returns None when missing or filtered out by ACL.

docs.title: resolve_nodes
docs.text:
Batch fetch by IDs (order preserved; missing slots are None):

await PostType.resolve_nodes(info=info, node_ids=["…", "…"])

Also used internally by RelationAccessFilter when falling back from a foreign key on mutation to_type paths.

docs.title: resolve_list
docs.text:
Offset/limit listing with filters, ordering, and optional total count:

@strawberry.field
async def list(
    self,
    info: Info,
    limit: int | None = None,
    offset: int | None = None,
    filters: PostFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET,
) -> ListResult[PostType]:
    return await PostType.resolve_list(
        info=info,
        limit=limit,
        offset=offset,
        filters=filters,
    )

Extra keyword arguments are forwarded to QueryOptimizer.optimize_query (order=, return_total_count=, access_filter=, …).

docs.title: resolve_connection
docs.text:
Relay connection pagination (after / before / first / last) with totalCount:

@strawberry.field
async def connection(
    self,
    info: Info,
    after: str | None = None,
    before: str | None = None,
    first: int | None = None,
    last: int | None = None,
    filters: PostFilter | None = strawberry.UNSET,
) -> OptimizedListConnection[PostType]:
    return await PostType.resolve_connection(
        info=info,
        after=after,
        before=before,
        first=first,
        last=last,
        filters=filters,
    )

docs.title: Per-call ACL
docs.text: All four resolvers accept access_filter= to override the type ClassVar for that call only. Use this for admin/ elevating views without forking the GraphQL type.

docs.title: Using QueryOptimizer directly
docs.text:
When you need a custom path (shared session, manual mapping), construct the optimizer yourself:

from strawberry_alchemy import QueryOptimizer, map_sqlalchemy_list_to_types


async def _get_optimized_result(cls, info: Info, **kwargs):
    session = await info.context.get_shared_session()  # app-specific
    optimizer = QueryOptimizer(info, session)
    optimizer.register_access_filter(cls.model_class, cls.access_filter)
    result = await optimizer.optimize_query(
        cls.model_class,
        strawberry_type=cls,
        **kwargs,
    )
    items = await map_sqlalchemy_list_to_types(
        result.items, info, cls, result.selected_fields
    )
    return result, items

See Recipes: shared vs tenant sessions.

docs.title: Pagination notes
docs.text:
• Prefer Relay connections for infinite scroll; use ListResult for simple admin tables.
  • Configure StrawberryConfig(relay_max_results=…) on the schema to cap connection page size.
  • Soft-deleted rows are not filtered by the optimizer itself — apply deleted_at IS NULL in your AccessControlFilter or repository list helpers when needed.

docs.title: Query optimizer
docs.text:
QueryOptimizer is the core of the library. It reads info.selected_fields, compiles them into load options and annotations, applies filters and ACL, and returns a QueryResult.

from strawberry_alchemy import QueryOptimizer, QueryResult

optimizer = QueryOptimizer(info, session)
optimizer.register_access_filter(Post, PostAccessFilter)
result: QueryResult = await optimizer.optimize_query(
    Post,
    filters=filters,
    limit=limit,
    offset=offset,
    return_total_count=True,
    strawberry_type=PostType,
)
# result.items, result.selected_fields, result.total_count

BaseNodeType.resolve_* constructs this for you. Use the class directly when you need a custom session, mapping path, or subclass (custom order expressions).

docs.title: What it does automatically
docs.text: Behavior Effect Column deferral Unrequested scalar columns are defer()'d Relationship loading Selected relations use selectinload (with nested ACL when registered) Access control Registered AccessControlFilter on root + nested loads Filters / order / limit Via optimize_query kwargs Hints @optimize_field dependencies merge into the load plan

docs.title: @optimize_field hints
docs.text:
Decorate computed Strawberry fields so the optimizer knows what SQL to emit before the resolver runs.

from strawberry_alchemy import (
    AnnotateAncestry,
    AnnotateAnyExists,
    AnnotateCount,
    AnnotateCustom,
    AnnotateExists,
    PrefetchRelated,
    SelectColumns,
    optimize_field,
)

docs.title: PrefetchRelated
docs.text:
Eager-load a relationship (optionally a subset of fields, a SQL filter, and an edge ACL):

@strawberry.field
@optimize_field(PrefetchRelated("cover_images", filter=lambda rel: rel.c.is_primary.is_(True)))
async def cover_thumb_url(self, info: Info) -> str | None:
    ...

Constructor: PrefetchRelated(relationship, fields=None, filter_current_user=False, filter=None, access_filter=None).

Shorthand: @optimize_field("comments") ≡ PrefetchRelated("comments").

docs.title: SelectColumns
docs.text:
Undefer same-row scalar columns needed by a computed field:

@optimize_field(SelectColumns("storage_key", "bucket"))
async def public_url(self, info: Info) -> str:
    ...

docs.title: AnnotateExists / AnnotateAnyExists
docs.text:
Correlated EXISTS → boolean attribute (default _comments_exists from relationship name):

@strawberry.field
@optimize_field(AnnotateExists("comments"))
async def has_comments(self, info: Info) -> bool:
    return bool(getattr(self, "_comments_exists", False))

AnnotateAnyExists(["a", "b"]) ORs multiple EXISTS checks.

docs.title: AnnotateCount
docs.text:
Correlated COUNT annotation:

@optimize_field(AnnotateCount("comments"))
async def comment_count(self, info: Info) -> int:
    return int(getattr(self, "_comments_count", 0))

docs.title: AnnotateCustom
docs.text:
Attach an arbitrary SQL expression (optional mapper to transform the value):

@optimize_field(AnnotateCustom("comments", expression=..., to_attr="_custom", mapper=...))

docs.title: AnnotateAncestry
docs.text:
Recursive parent-walk CTE for trees:

AnnotateAncestry(
    "parent",
    parent_field="parent_id",
    id_field="id",
    value_mode="ids",  # or "chain"
    include_self=True,
    root_first=True,
)

Dialect-aware aggregates; useful for breadcrumbs / path queries.

docs.title: Combining hints
docs.text:
Pass multiple hints to one decorator:

@optimize_field(
    PrefetchRelated("media"),
    SelectColumns("slug"),
    AnnotateCount("likes"),
)
async def card(self, info: Info) -> Card:
    ...

docs.title: Subclassing for custom order
docs.text:
Override process_order when sort keys are computed expressions rather than plain columns:

class PropertyQueryOptimizer(QueryOptimizer):
    def process_order(self, model, order_input):
        # return (order_by_list, extra_dependency_tree)
        ...

See Recipes.

docs.title: QueryAnalyzer
docs.text:
Optional diagnostics. Enable with env QUERY_ANALYZER_ENABLED=1, or pass an instance:

from strawberry_alchemy import QueryAnalyzer, QueryOptimizer

analyzer = QueryAnalyzer(
    log_sql=True,
    on_report=lambda report: metrics.emit(report.as_dict()),
)
optimizer = QueryOptimizer(info, session, analyzer=analyzer)

QueryReport exposes .summary() / .as_dict() for logging or OpenTelemetry export via on_report.

docs.title: Selection-tree helpers
docs.text:
Advanced tooling re-exported at the package root:

Helper Role parse_selection_tree Raw selection dict → typed tree FieldPath / FieldSelection / LeafSelection / RelayConnectionSelection Typed nodes extract_at_path Drill into a selection by path selection_to_model_fields Tree → model field dict build_recursive_dependency_tree / merge_dependency_trees / normalize_dependency_fields / source_path_to_dependency_tree Hint dependency merging

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text: Production patterns distilled from real apps using strawberry-alchemy. Snippets are anonymized and illustrative — adapt names to your domain.

docs.title: Project repository subclass
docs.text:
Wrap BaseRepository once for SAVEPOINT + conflict mapping so domain code stays thin:

from typing import ClassVar

from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from strawberry_alchemy import BaseRepository, NotFoundError as RepoNotFoundError


class ConflictError(Exception):
    ...


class AppRepository(BaseRepository[ModelT, SchemaT]):
    model_cls: ClassVar[type]
    schema_cls: ClassVar[type]

    async def create(self, schema, should_commit=True):
        try:
            async with self.session.begin_nested():
                return await super().create(schema, should_commit=False)
        except IntegrityError as exc:
            raise ConflictError(...) from exc
        finally:
            if should_commit:
                await self.session.commit()

Callers then use EmploymentRepository(session) with ClassVar model_cls / schema_cls / relation_models already set. Alias NotFoundError at the boundary so GraphQL layers do not depend on the library exception name.

docs.title: Deletion policy layer
docs.text:
Build soft-vs-hard decisions and audit on top of BaseDeletionHandler instead of a second protocol:

class EmploymentDeletionHandler(BaseDeletionHandler[Employment]):
    async def collect_dependents(self, session, entity_id, instance) -> DependentMap:
        ...

    async def handle_cascade(self, session, entity_id, dependents) -> None:
        ...


async def delete_employment(repo, employment_id, *, hard: bool):
    if hard:
        report = await repo.delete(id=employment_id, strict=True)
        audit("hard_delete", report)
        return report
    return await repo.soft_delete(id=employment_id)

Keep cascade SQL inside the handler; keep product policy (when hard is allowed) in the application service.

docs.title: App tenancy vs Alchemy ACL
docs.text:
Layer Mechanism Owns GraphQL row ACL AccessControlFilter / RelationAccessFilter “What this user may see in this API” DB tenancy Postgres RLS GUCs / bind_company-style helpers “What this connection may touch at all”

Typical flow:

  1. Bind tenant GUCs at session/transaction start (apply_rls_context or your own SET helper).
  2. Keep Alchemy ACL for people-scope / ownership rules that RLS does not encode.
  3. When resolving nested fields that join another tenant's data, rebind GUCs for that tenant before running the nested optimizer query.
  4. Do not nest db_execution_lock acquisitions — take the lock once per DB burst.

docs.title: When to use RelationAccessFilter
docs.text:
Use the type-level access_filter for the default visibility of a model. Add RelationAccessFilter on a field when one edge must be wider or narrower:

  • Employment list: people-scope ACL
  • employment.manager: still readable for reporting line even if that person is outside the viewer's people scope
manager: PersonType | None = strawberry.field(
    default=strawberry.UNSET,
    extensions=[RelationAccessFilter(ManagerAccessFilter, foreign_key="manager_id")],
)

Prefer PrefetchRelated(..., access_filter=...) when the edge is loaded only for a computed field, not as a normal GraphQL relation.

docs.title: Non-column / tab filters
docs.text:
Office UIs often expose a single listTab enum. Map it through CUSTOM_FILTERS:

def _list_tab_filter(model, value):
    if value == "NEEDS_APPROVAL":
        return model.status == "pending"
    if value == "MINE":
        return model.assignee_id == current_user_id_from_context()
    return True


class TravelType(BaseNodeType):
    CUSTOM_FILTERS = {"list_tab": _list_tab_filter}

Keep the GraphQL input field name aligned with the dict key (list_tab).

docs.title: Custom order columns
docs.text:
Subclass QueryOptimizer when sort keys are expressions:

class ListingQueryOptimizer(QueryOptimizer):
    def process_order(self, model, order_input):
        if order_input and order_input.field == "priceSale":
            expr = case((model.listing_type == "sale", model.price), else_=None)
            direction = asc if order_input.direction == Ordering.ASC else desc
            return [direction(expr)], {}
        return super().process_order(model, order_input)

Validate that required filters are present when an order key only makes sense for a subset of rows (e.g. sale vs rent).

docs.title: Field optimization toolkit
docs.text:
Common production combo on card / list types:

@strawberry.field
@optimize_field(
    PrefetchRelated("media", filter=lambda m: m.c.kind == "cover"),
    SelectColumns("storage_key", "width", "height"),
    AnnotateCount("favorites"),
)
async def card(self, info: Info) -> CardPayload:
    ...
  • PrefetchRelated — avoid N+1 on related rows needed only for the computed field
  • SelectColumns — undefer scalars the card needs even if the client did not select them as GraphQL fields
  • AnnotateCount / AnnotateExists — cheap aggregates without loading collections

docs.title: Mutations: inject actor / tenant
docs.text:
GraphQL inputs rarely include actor_user_id / company_id. Inject via kwargs:

cmd = schema_from_input(
    CreateEmploymentCommand,
    input,
    actor_user_id=user.id,
    company_id=ctx.company_id,
)

Same pattern with PostSchema.from_input(input, user_id=user.id).

docs.title: Shared vs tenant sessions
docs.text:
Catalog entities (global users, countries) may live on a shared database while tenant data uses RLS-bound sessions. Override the optimized-result path on those types:

@classmethod
async def _get_optimized_result(cls, info, **kwargs):
    session = await info.context.get_shared_session()
    optimizer = QueryOptimizer(info, session)
    optimizer.register_access_filter(cls.model_class, cls.access_filter)
    return await optimizer.optimize_query(cls.model_class, strawberry_type=cls, **kwargs)

(Exact hook name depends on whether you subclass BaseNodeType methods or wrap resolve_list — keep session choice next to the type that owns the data.)

docs.title: Boundary exception aliasing
docs.text:
At GraphQL / HTTP boundaries:

from strawberry_alchemy import NotFoundError as RepoNotFoundError

try:
    return await repo.get_by_id(id)
except RepoNotFoundError:
    raise GraphQLNotFound(...)

Keeps library types out of API error schemas while staying explicit at the import.

docs.title: Repository
docs.text: BaseRepository is a generic async CRUD layer over AsyncSession. Pair it with BaseSchema so you can move data both ways: schema → DB row and DB row → schema.

docs.title: Declaring a repository
docs.text:
from typing import ClassVar
from strawberry_alchemy import BaseRepository

from .models import Comment, Post
from .schemas import CommentSchema, PostSchema


class PostRepository(BaseRepository[Post, PostSchema]):
    model_cls: ClassVar[type[Post]] = Post
    schema_cls: ClassVar[type[PostSchema]] = PostSchema
    relation_models: ClassVar[dict[str, type]] = {"comments": Comment}
    soft_delete_field: ClassVar[str | None] = "deleted_at"

With ClassVars set: PostRepository(session). You can still pass model_cls= / schema_cls= to the constructor for one-off use.

Optional: deletion_handler=PostDeletionHandler() for cascade / cleanup on delete().

docs.title: CRUD
docs.text:
Method Behavior get_by_id(id, *, include_deleted=False) Load one; raises NotFoundError if missing get_by_ids(ids, *, include_deleted=False) Batch load create(schema, should_commit=True) Insert from schema dump update(schema, should_commit=True, instance=None) Patch by schema.id delete(id, *, strict=False) Hard delete → DeletionReport soft_delete(id) Sets soft_delete_field timestamp add_related / remove_related M2M / collection membership via relation_models

apply_not_deleted(stmt) adds the soft-delete predicate when soft_delete_field is configured.

repo = PostRepository(session)
created = await repo.create(schema=PostSchema(user_id=..., title="Hi", body="…"))
updated = await repo.update(schema=PostSchema(id=created.id, user_id=..., title="Yo", body="…"))
await repo.soft_delete(id=updated.id)

docs.title: Soft delete
docs.text:
1. Mix SoftDeleteMixin into the model (or add your own deleted_at column).
  2. Set soft_delete_field = "deleted_at" on the repository.
  3. Prefer soft_delete() for user-facing deletes; use delete() for hard cascades / admin cleanup.
  4. Mirror the predicate in AccessControlFilter if list/node queries should hide soft-deleted rows.

docs.title: Deletion reports and handlers
docs.text:
delete() returns a DeletionReport instead of raising on every soft failure:

report = await repo.delete(id=post_id, strict=False)
if report.has_failures:
    ...  # inspect report.failures / DeletionPartialFailure

strict=True raises when the handler reports failures.

docs.title: BaseDeletionHandler
docs.text:
from strawberry_alchemy import BaseDeletionHandler, DependentMap


class PostDeletionHandler(BaseDeletionHandler[Post]):
    async def collect_dependents(self, session, entity_id, instance) -> DependentMap:
        ...
        return {"comments": list(comment_ids)}

    async def handle_cascade(self, session, entity_id, dependents: DependentMap) -> None:
        ...

DependentMap is dict[str, list[uuid.UUID]]. Collect first, then cascade (and optionally block delete based on dependents in an app-level policy — see Recipes).

docs.title: Base (SQLAlchemy)
docs.text:
strawberry_alchemy.models.Base is an abstract declarative base aimed at Postgres:

  • UUID primary key (sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.UUID)
  • created_at / updated_at (DateTime(timezone=True) with server defaults)
  • Automatic __tablename__ from the class name (Post → post)
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from strawberry_alchemy import Base


class Post(Base):
    user_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(UUID(as_uuid=True), ForeignKey("user.id"))
    title: Mapped[str]
    body: Mapped[str]

Non-Postgres databases

For SQLite (tests) or other dialects, define your own DeclarativeBase with sqlalchemy.Uuid (or equivalent) and the same column names. The blog example does this. GraphQL types and the optimizer only require those columns to exist on the mapped class — they do not require library Base.

docs.title: SoftDeleteMixin
docs.text:
Adds a nullable, indexed deleted_at column. Pair it with BaseRepository.soft_delete_field = "deleted_at" so get_by_id / list queries exclude soft-deleted rows by default and soft_delete() works.

from strawberry_alchemy import SoftDeleteMixin

class Post(SoftDeleteMixin, Base):
    ...

docs.title: BaseNodeType
docs.text:
Relay Node GraphQL type that owns the read path into the optimizer.

Built-in fields: id (NodeID[UUID]), created_at, updated_at (default strawberry.UNSET).

Required ClassVar

ClassVar Purpose access_filter AccessControlFilter subclass (or instance) — sets model_class

Optional ClassVars

ClassVar Purpose CUSTOM_FILTERS dict[str, Callable] — non-column filter keys → SQL clause builders model_class Filled from access_filter.model_class

Declare selected columns and relationships as Strawberry fields defaulting to UNSET. Nested types often use strawberry.lazy to break cycles.

@strawberry.type
class PostType(BaseNodeType):
    access_filter: ClassVar[type[PostAccessFilter]] = PostAccessFilter

    title: str | None = strawberry.UNSET
    comments: list[CommentType] | None = strawberry.UNSET

docs.title: Construction helpers
docs.text:
• PostType.from_schema(schema, **overrides) — build from a BaseSchema / Pydantic model (nested schemas become related Strawberry types).
  • Schema side: schema.to_type(PostType) prefers from_schema when available.

Offset/limit list wrapper:

@strawberry.type
class ListResult[T]:

docs.title: Relay connection types
docs.text:
Symbol Role OptimizedListConnection[NodeType] Connection with edges, page_info, total_count Edge / PageInfo Re-exported from strawberry.relay SliceMetadata Cursor / first / last → start / end / fetch_limit math

resolve_connection on BaseNodeType delegates to OptimizedListConnection.resolve_connection, which uses the same optimizer path as lists.

docs.title: Ordering
docs.text:
from strawberry_alchemy import Ordering  # enum: ASC, DESC

Pass order inputs through to resolve_list / resolve_connection / QueryOptimizer.optimize_query as your app's order input shape; the optimizer maps known model columns (and subclasses can override process_order — see Recipes).
